title: Rental housing review and climate progress
subtitle: Eby Farm playground, asset management plan, indoor space strategy, Meadowsweet Avenue purchase and Beaver Creek engineering contract.
overview: Council directed staff to review Waterloo's rental licensing rules and to research short-term rental licensing, a mid- and high-rise safety inspection program, and options to reduce renovictions. Staff will return with recommendations {{vote:m15}}. Tenants, students and landlords are expected to be consulted. Council also received the 2022 community greenhouse gas inventory, which showed the region is not on track for its 2030 target {{vote:m13}}.

Council approved several spending items: the Eby Farm accessible playground expansion {{vote:m8}}, the purchase of 714 Meadowsweet Avenue {{vote:m12}}, and engineering services for Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive, including sanitary pumping stations {{vote:m11}}. It endorsed the 2024 Asset Management Plan, which reports an average annual infrastructure funding gap of $54.3 million {{vote:m9}}. It also approved the Indoor Community Space Strategy in principle, with amendments on culturally appropriate engagement and arts space {{vote:m14}}.

Council met in closed session earlier in the day on labour matters and a possible sale of city-owned land. The minutes report no decisions from that session. Council agreed to attend the Regional All-Council Meeting on June 21 {{vote:m16}}.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to review rental licensing rules, research short-term rental licensing and a mid- and high-rise safety program, and explore tenant support and eviction-related options, then report back {{vote:m15}}.

Council approved the strategy in principle for the upcoming Sport, Recreation and Leisure Strategy, with two amended recommendations on culturally appropriate engagement and prioritizing arts and creative space {{vote:m14}}.
Council endorsed the plan, acknowledged the $54.3 million average annual funding gap, and directed staff to keep advocating for climate and infrastructure grants {{vote:m9}}.
Council awarded the tender to Lyncon Construction Inc. for a total of $793,810.15 and approved $700,000 in project transfers to the accessible playground project {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved buying the property for $650,000 plus taxes and closing costs, and released $750,000 from the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve {{vote:m12}}.

decisions.item: Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive
decisions.detail: Council awarded design, tendering, contract administration and inspection services to Stantec Consulting Ltd. for a total of $2,647,933 {{vote:m11}}.
Council received the 2022 Region of Waterloo greenhouse gas inventory report for information {{vote:m13}}.

debate: On the Eby Farm playground, an accessibility advisory delegate said the committee was consulted early and again before tender, and welcomed the result. An accessible swing was left out because it needs a large safety zone. Staff said it is on a list for a future project, and one councillor asked whether it should be prioritized. The park's hilltop washroom is to be demolished under a separate project.

On the greenhouse gas inventory, presenters said community emissions are below the 2010 baseline but the region is not on track for its 2030 target. Transportation and buildings are the main sources. Resident delegates urged more public mobilization, more frequent reporting and heat pump pilot projects. Staff described neighbourhood outreach, a planned small grant program and a website redesign.

On the indoor space strategy, one councillor proposed amendments so engagement is culturally appropriate and arts space is prioritized rather than only explored. Others raised the lack of city-run indoor facilities in the west end, the cost of renting space for community groups, and whether the indoor track meets local track clubs' needs. Staff said these would be examined in the upcoming Sport, Recreation and Leisure Strategy.

On rental housing, student delegates described maintenance problems, overcrowding and a heat warning in effect that day. They said waits at the Landlord and Tenant Board are too long for students on short work terms. Staff said an eviction permit program might overlap with provincial rules and could face legal challenge, so education and support for tenants are also proposed. Councillors asked about consultation, how fourplexes and owner-occupied units would be treated, and advocating to the province.
